state.question: Why do resonator_lab trials 21–23 (days 10) show elevated cycles/beat relative to baseline, and is this a calibration drift or measurement artifact?

hypotheses.label: Normal statistical variation within expected measurement precision
hypotheses.rationale: With only 23 trials total, baseline mean 2.6984 cycles/beat has inherent uncertainty. Trials 21–23 show 2.7077, 2.7304, 2.7364 — roughly +0.01 to +0.04 above mean. Without knowing measurement uncertainty (which should be established but isn't documented here), these could be tail events of the baseline distribution. Pendulum_lab shows similar scatter around its mean throughout all 48 trials with no obvious trend.

hypotheses.rationale: Three consecutive elevated readings (events 174, 175, 176) after prior trials stayed closer to baseline mean could indicate instrument drift. Trial 20 (event 128, day 7) showed 2.7073, close to trial 21's value, possibly marking drift onset. However, trial 19 (event 127, day 7) was 2.6610, below mean, so pattern is not monotonic. Only 5 post-day-6 resonator trials exist; need more data to distinguish drift from variance.

hypotheses.label: Environmental or procedural change affecting resonator_lab on day 10
hypotheses.rationale: All three day-10 resonator trials elevated together could reflect changed conditions (temperature, humidity, operator technique, timing protocol). However, no corresponding shift visible in pendulum_lab trials from days 5–9, which sample throughout the period. Pendulum_lab trial 48 (event 162, day 9) shows 1.6756, unremarkable. Lack of correlated effect across labs weakens this explanation.

beliefTimeline.summaryOfChange: New question identified: resonator_lab's three most recent trials (day 10) all exceed baseline mean, whereas pendulum_lab shows no trend across its 48 trials. This is the first observable departure from baseline noise in either instrument. Probabilities favor mundane explanations (statistical variation 0.45, calibration drift 0.30) over environmental causes given lack of cross-lab correlation. Critical next step: continue resonator trials to distinguish trend from variance, and verify resonator calibration against known standard.
